chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Regarding a man who was told to him, 'You did such and such,' and he said, 'By Allah, I did not do it,' while he had indeed done it, he said: 'It is a lie; he lied about it, so he seeks forgiveness from Allah for it.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a false oath of denial when the accused actually committed the act?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of a false oath (*kathibah*) taken to refute a true accusation, emphasizing that the mere utterance of the lie incurs the need for repentance (*istighfar*). It highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the spiritual consequence of perjury, distinguishing between the factual truth of the act and the moral weight of the sworn denial. The ruling underscores the importance of sincerity in oaths and the immediate accountability for verbal falsehoods before Allah.
